references.text: Hagar is asked, "Where do you come from, and where are you going?" - the same type of question about origin and destination.
Abraham lifted his eyes and saw men who needed hospitality, in the same way as the old man lifted his eyes and saw the traveler.
Lot sees the travelers in the city square and offers hospitality, parallel to the old man's action in Gibeah.
Abraham's servant asks Rebekah about her origin, similar questions about where one comes from.
Jacob instructs his servants to answer the question, "Who do you belong to, and where are you going?"
Joshua asks the Gibeonites, "Who are you, and where do you come from?" - the same type of interrogation of strangers.
David asks the Egyptian slave, "Who do you belong to, and where do you come from?"
The Lord asks Satan, "Where do you come from?" - a similar question about origin.
The Lord again asks Satan where he comes from.
